summary: Notes 7–8 describe ExxonMobil’s equity companies, including their industries and regions, related-party sales shares for 2020–2022, investment valuation and amortization, and upstream impairments. They provide summarized equity-company financial results and ExxonMobil’s share for 2020–2022, plus significant ventures and ownership percentages at year-end 2022 across upstream and product businesses. Investments, advances, securities, and long-term receivables are reported for 2021 and 2022, including applicable allowances and reserves.

title: 9. Property, Plant and Equipment and Asset Retirement Obligations
summary: The note presents property, plant and equipment cost and net balances by business segment for 2022 and 2021, and describes impairment charges: $6.4 billion in 2022, including $4.5 billion related to exiting Sakhalin-1; $1.2 billion in 2021; and $25.9 billion in 2020, mainly from abandoning dry-gas development. It identifies income-statement lines where impairments are recorded and accumulated depreciation. It explains asset-retirement-obligation measurement, accounting, assumptions and Product Solutions site uncertainties; provides 2020–2022 liability activity, long-term balances, and estimated 2023–2024 cash payments.

title: 10. Accounting for Suspended Exploratory Well Costs
summary: Explains the criteria for continuing to capitalize exploratory well costs and presents 2020–2022 changes in capitalized balances, aging categories, and project counts. Of 26 projects with costs capitalized for over a year at year-end 2022, 11 had recent or planned exploration; the other 15, totaling $2.324 billion, are progressing toward development. A country-by-country table lists these projects, capitalized amounts, drilling/acquisition years, and development status or plans.

title: 11. Leases
key_items: Lease Cost; Balance Sheet; Right of use assets
Total lease payments; Total lease liability; Other Information; Cash paid for amounts included in the measurement of lease liabilities; Noncash right of use assets recorded for lease liabilities
Cash paid for amounts included in the measurement of lease liabilities
Noncash right of use assets recorded for lease liabilities
summary: Notes 11–12 describe lease accounting and related figures, plus earnings per share. Leases are mainly operating leases for equipment and facilities; qualifying leases are recognized using discounted fixed payments and affiliate borrowing rates, while lessor activity and variable payments, guarantees, restrictions, covenants, and related-party transactions are insignificant. Tables report 2020–2022 lease costs, balance-sheet assets and liabilities, terms and discount rates, 2022 payment maturities, uncommenced commitments, lease types, cash flows, and noncash additions. EPS data for 2020–2022 includes attributable net income or loss, weighted-average shares, EPS (diluted results are identical), and dividends per share.

title: 13. Financial Instruments and Derivatives
summary: The notes present fair-value measurements and hierarchy levels for financial instruments and derivatives at December 31, 2022 and 2021, including asset and liability categories, balance-sheet classifications, valuation methods for equity-company balances and contingent consideration, and collateral held under master netting arrangements. They describe derivative risk management, trading and income-statement presentation, the immateriality of currency and interest-rate derivatives, counterparty controls, net commodity derivative positions, and realized and unrealized derivative gains or losses by income-statement line for 2020–2022.

title: 14. Long-Term Debt
summary: At year-end 2022, long-term debt was $40.559 billion, including $34.507 billion payable in U.S. dollars and $6.052 billion equivalent in foreign currencies; $181 million due within one year was classified as current. Debt was extinguished after cash was irrevocably deposited to redeem two 2023 notes. Excluding finance leases, maturities for 2024–2027 are $4.665 billion, $4.667 billion, $3.644 billion, and $1.090 billion; unused long-term credit lines totaled $1.2 billion. The company designated $4.8 billion of euro debt and accrued interest as a perfectly effective hedge of its European net investment, with exchange changes recorded in accumulated other comprehensive income. The debt table compares 2022 and 2021 balances and rates for Corporation U.S.- and euro-denominated notes, XTO senior notes, industrial revenue bonds, finance leases and other obligations, and debt issuance costs; it also notes premiums and average effective or imputed rates.

title: 15. Incentive Program
summary: The 2003 Incentive Program permits options, SARs, restricted stock and other awards for eligible employees and qualifying affiliates. Options/SARs are granted at no less than market value and last up to 10 years; the 220-million-share limit excludes forfeited, expired or cash-settled awards. The plan has no fixed term, may be ended by the Board, and had 60 million shares available at year-end 2022. Restricted awards, their eligibility, forfeiture terms, stock- or cash-settlement accounting, grant activity, vesting schedules and 2022 outstanding-share rollforward are detailed. The note also reports grant-date values, compensation expense and tax benefits, unrecognized cost and recognition period, vested fair values, and cash settlement payments for 2020–2022.

title: 16. Litigation and Other Contingencies
summary: Notes cover litigation and other contingencies: ExxonMobil’s loss-accrual and disclosure policies, its view that pending lawsuits will not materially harm the company, guarantees and other obligations at year-end 2022, and long-term commitments. They also detail pension and postretirement benefit assumptions, obligations, assets, funding status, balance-sheet and comprehensive-income recognition, periodic costs, contributions and expected payments, investment strategy, and 2021–2022 fair values by asset category and valuation hierarchy, including underfunded plans and Medicare subsidies.

title: 18. Disclosures about Segments and Related Information
summary: The note identifies Upstream, Energy Products, Chemical Products, and Specialty Products as reportable segments based on their activities, management review, and available financial information, and describes each segment’s business. It explains that after-tax earnings include transfers at estimated market prices and gives Corporate and Financing interest details, including non-debt interest expense for 2020–2022. It presents segment and corporate financial measures for 2020–2022, including earnings, equity-company earnings, revenues, expenses, taxes, capital additions, investments, and assets, by U.S. and non-U.S. operations where applicable; figures may not sum exactly due to rounding.

title: Revenue and Geographic Information
summary: Explains that operating revenue includes ASC 606 customer-contract revenue and primarily physically settled commodity derivatives outside ASC 606, with similar contract terms and customers. Tables report revenue by accounting scope and year, geographic sales for the United States and non-U.S. markets, and significant non-U.S. country sources, with an attribution caveat. Geographic long-lived assets are also shown for the United States and non-U.S. regions, including major non-U.S. countries, across the reported years.

title: Federal and non-U.S.
summary: The notes detail 2020–2022 income taxes by jurisdiction and type, other taxes and duties, deferred-tax provision effects, and the 2022 EU energy-sector surplus-profits tax and its $1.8 billion charge. They reconcile reported taxes to the 21% theoretical U.S. rate and report effective rates. They explain deferred-tax assets, liabilities, valuation allowances, balance-sheet classification, and indefinitely reinvested foreign earnings. They also describe uncertain tax positions, annual balance changes, litigation and audit exposures, open examination years, possible near-term changes, and tax-related interest and penalties.

title: 20. Divestment Activities
key_items: SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION ON OIL AND GAS EXPLORATION AND PRODUCTION ACTIVITIES (unaudited)
summary: The notes report 2022 divestitures: about $5 billion in proceeds and $0.4 billion in after-tax earnings, plus pending California and Nigerian asset sales, their approval or legal conditions, and potential losses. Supplemental unaudited oil-and-gas producing-activity results for 2022, 2021, and 2020 are presented by region for consolidated subsidiaries and equity companies, covering sales, transfers, revenue, costs, taxes, and results. The text explains excluded Upstream activities and their yearly totals and notes that oil sands mining is included.

title: Oil and Gas Exploration and Production Costs
summary: The text explains that consolidated subsidiaries’ net capitalized costs are $10.785 billion lower in 2022 and $12.005 billion lower in 2021 than Upstream PP&E investments because certain transportation, research, and LNG assets are excluded; oil sands and oil shale mining assets are included under FASB rules. It then presents 2022 and 2021 regional tables for the United States, Canada/Other Americas, Europe, Africa, Australia/Oceania, Asia, and total, detailing consolidated-subsidiary and equity-company property costs, producing assets, construction in progress, total capitalized costs, accumulated depreciation and depletion, and net capitalized costs.

title: Oil and Gas Exploration and Production Costs (continued)

nodes.title: Costs Incurred in Property Acquisitions, Exploration and Development Activities
nodes.summary: Explains that costs incurred include capitalized and expensed amounts, new asset-retirement obligations, and obligation adjustments from revised estimates or abandonment dates. Consolidated costs rose to $14.513 billion in 2022, mainly from higher development costs; they fell to $9.877 billion in 2021 from 2020, mainly due to lower development costs, partly offset by higher unproved-property acquisitions. Equity-company costs increased to $1.769 billion in 2022 due to development spending. The table details 2020–2022 acquisition, exploration, and development costs by activity, region, and consolidated subsidiaries versus equity companies.

nodes.title: Oil and Gas Reserves
nodes.summary: Defines proved reserves under SEC rules, including economic, contractual, pricing, and estimation criteria; explains revisions, ownership and exclusions, production-sharing effects, developed/undeveloped reserves, and production-volume differences. Reports that production-sharing contracts represented 12% of 2022 proved reserves. Summarizes reserve changes: 2022 production, sales, downward revisions including Russia, and additions from purchases, extensions, and discoveries; 2021 additions from price-driven bitumen revisions and discoveries; and 2020 price- and capital-spending-related downward revisions.

nodes.title: Crude Oil, Natural Gas Liquids, Bitumen and Synthetic Oil Proved Reserves
nodes.summary: Tables report ExxonMobil’s proved crude oil, natural gas liquids, bitumen, and synthetic oil reserves in millions of barrels. They show 2020–2022 reserve movements for consolidated subsidiaries and equity-company interests, including revisions, improved recovery, purchases, sales, discoveries/extensions, production, noncontrolling interests, and year-end totals, broken down by region and product. Additional tables classify year-end 2020–2022 liquids reserves as developed or undeveloped and by ownership. Notes identify Russian reserves expropriated in 2022 and refer readers to the 2022 Form 10-K for NGL details.

nodes.title: Natural Gas and Oil-Equivalent Proved Reserves
nodes.summary: Tables report proved natural-gas reserves by region and total oil-equivalent reserves for 2020–2022, including annual changes from revisions, improved recovery, purchases, sales, extensions/discoveries and production. They show consolidated subsidiaries’ reserves, noncontrolling interests, equity-company interests, and total reserves, plus developed and undeveloped reserve breakdowns by ownership type and year-end. Natural gas is converted at six billion cubic feet per million barrels; 2022 revisions include Russia expropriations.

summary: Covers 2020–2022 oil and gas acquisition, exploration, and development costs, including capitalized and expensed amounts and asset-retirement obligations, with comparisons by activity, region, and ownership. Defines proved reserves and explains estimation criteria, revisions, ownership, production-sharing contracts, and developed versus undeveloped reserves. Tables detail annual movements and year-end crude oil, NGL, bitumen, synthetic oil, and natural gas reserves by product, region, and ownership, including production, discoveries, purchases, sales, revisions, and Russia-related expropriations; gas is converted to oil-equivalent volumes.

title: Standardized Measure of Discounted Future Cash Flows
key_items: Standardized Measure of Discounted Future Cash Flows
summary: Explains that the FASB-required standardized measure discounts future net cash flows from proved reserves at 10%, using first-day-of-month average prices, year-end costs, and legislated tax rates, and includes future dismantlement, abandonment, and rehabilitation costs. The Corporation cautions that the measure is not a reliable estimate of expected cash flows or reserve value, since prescribed assumptions—particularly point-in-time prices—can cause significant year-to-year variability. A table is titled “Standardized Measure of Discounted Future Cash Flows” and is denominated in millions of dollars.

title: As of December 31, 2020 Consolidated Subsidiaries
summary: Presents ExxonMobil’s standardized measure of discounted future oil and gas cash flows, in millions of dollars, for 2020–2022. For consolidated subsidiaries and equity companies, it reports by region and total future oil and gas sales, production and development costs, income taxes, net cash flows, the effect of discounting at 10%, and discounted net cash flows. A footnote identifies discounted cash flows attributable to noncontrolling interests in Canada/Other Americas for 2020, 2021, and 2022.

title: Changes in Discounted Future Cash Flows from Proved Reserves
key_items: Change in Standardized Measure of Discounted Future Net Cash Flows Relating to Proved Oil and Gas Reserves
summary: Reports annual changes in the standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows from proved oil and gas reserves for 2020–2022, in millions of dollars. For consolidated subsidiaries, equity-method investees, and their combined total, it shows beginning and ending values and changes from reserve additions, production, development costs, prices and costs, reserve-estimate revisions, discount accretion, and income taxes.

title: INDEX TO EXHIBITS
summary: The text lists ExxonMobil Form 10-K exhibits, including corporate governing documents, stock description, incentive and benefit plans, ethics code, subsidiaries, audit consent, officer certifications, and Inline XBRL files; identifies compensatory exhibits; and notes debt instruments will be supplied to the SEC upon request. It contains the report’s execution, power of attorney, and director/officer signatures dated February 22, 2023. It also sets out 2022 restricted stock unit terms: award acceptance and crediting, vesting dates, transfer limits, forfeiture, taxes, settlement, dividend equivalents, capitalization adjustments, legal limits, data privacy, no employment or future-award guarantees, governing law, jurisdiction, and entire agreement.

title: EXXONMOBIL SUPPLEMENTAL SAVINGS PLAN
summary: The ExxonMobil Supplemental Savings Plan replaces employer Savings Plan contributions barred by Code limits 415 and 401(a)(17). It sets eligibility criteria, including qualifying retirement, certain asset sales or outsourcing, severance, or administrator discretion; describes monthly notional contribution credits, interest rates, calculation guidelines, and employee-contribution rules. Benefits are generally paid in a lump sum after applicable termination and waiting periods. It specifies death payments, beneficiary designations and default priorities, administration and interpretation authority, general-obligation status, restrictions on assignment, corporate amendment or termination rights, and forfeiture grounds including misconduct, criminal acts, unapproved early departure, or termination for cause.

title: EXXONMOBIL SUPPLEMENTAL PENSION PLAN
summary: The ExxonMobil Supplemental Pension Plan provides unfunded payments to make up pension benefits limited by tax-code compensation and benefit caps. It defines eligibility, calculates benefits to restore the Pension Plan’s normal-form value (considering overseas benefits), applies specified pension offsets, and sets commencement dates, early-retirement reductions, lump-sum payment rules, and key-employee adjustments. It covers death benefits and beneficiary designations/default priorities, excludes certain survivor annuities, and establishes administration, general-obligation status, anti-assignment rules, corporate amendment or termination rights, and forfeiture grounds for misconduct, unauthorized early separation, or termination for cause.

title: EXXONMOBIL ADDITIONAL PAYMENTS PLAN
summary: The text details ExxonMobil’s Additional Payments Plan: eligibility, formulas, service and compensation calculations, offsets, payment timing and forms for incentive pensions and overseas makeup benefits; death and disability benefits; and administration, amendment, assignment and forfeiture rules. It also includes a 2023 restricted-stock award letter for a non-employee director, describing share rights, restrictions, vesting events and beneficiary designation, plus Exhibit 21’s list of subsidiaries, ownership percentages, jurisdictions and explanatory notes on subsidiary classification, omitted entities and equity-method investments.

title: CONSENT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM
summary: PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP consents to incorporating by reference its February 22, 2023 report on Exxon Mobil Corporation’s financial statements and internal control over financial reporting into specified Form S-3 and Form S-8 registration statements. The consent is signed in Dallas, Texas, on February 22, 2023.

title: Certification by Darren W. Woods Pursuant to Securities Exchange Act Rule 13a-14(a)
summary: Exxon Mobil CEO Darren W. Woods certifies under Exchange Act Rule 13a-14(a) that he reviewed the 2022 Form 10-K; it contains no materially misleading statements, and its financial information fairly presents the company’s condition, results, and cash flows. He describes management’s responsibility for designing and evaluating disclosure controls and financial reporting controls, reporting material control changes, and disclosing significant deficiencies, material weaknesses, and relevant fraud to auditors and the audit committee. Signed February 22, 2023.

title: Certification by Kathryn A. Mikells Pursuant to Securities Exchange Act Rule 13a-14(a)
summary: Exhibit 31.2 is Kathryn A. Mikells’s February 22, 2023 certification under Exchange Act Rule 13a-14(a), confirming her review of Exxon Mobil’s Form 10-K, its lack of material misstatements or omissions, and fair presentation of financial information. She describes officers’ responsibilities for designing, evaluating, and reporting on disclosure controls and internal financial controls, including material changes, and for informing auditors and the audit committee of significant control deficiencies, material weaknesses, and relevant fraud. Mikells signs as Senior Vice President and CFO.

title: Certification by Len M. Fox Pursuant to Securities Exchange Act Rule 13a-14(a)
summary: Exhibits 31.3 and 32.1–32.3 contain Exxon Mobil officers’ certifications dated February 22, 2023. Controller Len M. Fox certifies he reviewed the 2022 Form 10-K, that it is materially accurate and fairly presents financial results, and describes management’s duties concerning disclosure controls, financial reporting controls, evaluations, control changes, and reporting deficiencies, weaknesses, or fraud. CEO Darren W. Woods, CFO Kathryn A. Mikells, and Fox certify under Sarbanes-Oxley Section 906 that the report complies with securities-law filing requirements and fairly presents the company’s financial condition and operating results; signed originals are retained and available to the SEC upon request.
